method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP) 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease' (published 30 May 2026), 26 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13409200). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334) 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease' (published 4 September 2018), 12 claims; LICENCE: No open licence: free to read on PMC under the PMC Copyright Notice ('Articles from Blood are provided here courtesy of The American Society of Hematology'); treated as © American Society of Hematology (read at the PMC article page (Copyright and License information; PMC Copyright Notice)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every Australian 2026 claim (S1) unchanged and adds S2, the CDCN 2018 international consensus treatment guideline (paraphrased, hash-anchored), for the severity markers, response criteria, rituximab as a first-line alternative, steroid doses and escalation timing that S1 keeps in stripped tables or does not state. Europe PMC and NCBI refuse XML download for this article, so S2 was read from the PMC HTML page (tables stripped; figure legends kept); the text after the reference list was discarded. S2 is older than S1, which already reflects it; where they differ, both are shown. The 2023 HemaSphere iMCD position paper (CC BY-NC-ND) was also readable but is an ad hoc expert panel, not a consensus guideline, so it was not used. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Table 5 (diagnostic work-up), Table 7 (CDCN severity criteria) and Tables 9-10 (CDCN response criteria) are paraphrased from the row lines. S1 Tables 1-4, 6 and 8 were not extracted (ragged rows or merged cells).

claims.claim: **Lymphadenopathy is present in every case,** often with B symptoms (fever, weight loss, night sweats) in 52%–72%. Anasarca (oedema, ascites, pleural effusions) is common, at 78%.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **TAFRO is the aggressive end:** thrombocytopenia, anasarca, fever, marrow reticulin fibrosis, renal impairment and organomegaly, often with rapid multi-organ failure. Its nodes are usually small (<1.5 cm), ALP is raised and there is no polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Markers of severity** include interstitial pneumonitis, severe renal dysfunction and haemoglobin ≤80 g/L; ECOG status decides urgency and whether the patient needs hospital, often high-dependency care.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected iMCD: refer to haematology,** then review the diagnosis and plan at a multidisciplinary team meeting once work-up is done.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe iMCD (CDCN), about 10% to 20% of patients:** organ failure such as renal failure, anasarca, severe anaemia or lung dysfunction with poor performance status, often needing critical care. Laboratory pointers are a very high CRP, albumin of 2.0 g/dL or less and platelets of 100 or less.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Major criteria:** lymphadenopathy in at least two nodal stations plus characteristic histology (regressed germinal centres and/or sheet-like polytypic plasmacytosis), best judged on an excisional biopsy.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HHV8 LANA-1 immunohistochemistry must be negative,** and infection, immune disease and malignancy must be excluded before the diagnosis is made.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use fine-needle aspiration to diagnose iMCD;** core biopsy is generally inferior to open excision.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Work-up:** CT or PET/CT for nodes, organomegaly, effusions and pneumonitis; FBC, creatinine/GFR, LFTs (albumin), immunoglobulins, ESR and CRP; test for HHV-8, EBV and uncontrolled infection. Bone marrow biopsy looks for malignancy, POEMS and TAFRO reticulin fibrosis.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Full work-up (S1 Table 5):** ask about B symptoms, fluid overload, skin changes such as eruptive cherry haemangiomas, and polyneuropathy (for POEMS). Bloods: FBC and film, electrolytes, calcium, phosphate, LDH, urate, liver tests with albumin, ESR, CRP, immunoglobulins, serum electrophoresis, immunofixation and free light chains; if available, IL-6, sIL-2R, VEGF and/or beta-2-microglobulin (the first three are not Medicare-rebated). Infection screen: HIV, hepatitis B and C, CMV, EBV and toxoplasma serology, a TB screen, blood HHV8/KSHV PCR and blood cultures. Exclusion serology: ANA, ENA and anti-dsDNA, complement C3 and C4, RF and anti-CCP, ANCA, antiphospholipid antibodies, direct Coombs test, ACE, ferritin and IgG subclasses. Urine protein- and albumin-creatinine ratios with electrophoresis and immunofixation; an excisional node biopsy (strongly preferred) and marrow aspirate and trephine; CT of neck, chest, abdomen and pelvis and FDG-PET/CT.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Main mimics:** POEMS (needs polyneuropathy and a monoclonal plasma cell disorder), SLE, Sjögren disease, RA, IgG4-related disease, sarcoidosis, Still disease, VEXAS and ANCA vasculitis. Autoantibodies occur in 30% of iMCD, so serology alone does not separate them.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **On PET-CT, a high standardised uptake value (above 6) should prompt a search for another diagnosis such as lymphoma** (CDCN).
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Do not use IL-6 levels to decide on treatment:** in the randomised siltuximab trial some patients with normal IL-6 responded and some with high IL-6 did not (CDCN).
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Grade severity by the CDCN criteria:** meeting at least two of the five means severe disease.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The five CDCN severity criteria (S1 Table 7):** ECOG performance status 2 or worse; stage IV kidney dysfunction (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m², or creatinine above 265 µmol/L); anasarca, ascites, or pleural or pericardial effusion; haemoglobin 80 g/L or lower; and lung involvement or interstitial pneumonitis with breathlessness.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Siltuximab is first line in both severe and non-severe iMCD** and is the only PBS-reimbursed drug for it. Standard dose: 11 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks. (Level II, Grade B)
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe disease: siltuximab plus high-dose steroid** (such as methylprednisolone 500 mg IV once a day for 3 days). Weekly siltuximab for 4 weeks has been suggested; critically unwell TAFRO patients may also get cyclosporin A.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic with normal organ function: no treatment,** but monitor, initially 6-weekly then 3-monthly, with history, exam, FBC, electrolytes, renal and liver tests and CRP. Treat promptly once symptoms or organ dysfunction appear.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptomatic non-severe disease:** siltuximab 11 mg/kg every 3 weeks with lower-dose steroid (for example prednisolone 1 mg/kg) for only 4–6 weeks while siltuximab takes effect; minimal symptoms can start siltuximab alone.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Responders stay on siltuximab indefinitely** (at least PR, until progression), with steroids weaned. Keep 3-weekly dosing where possible: 6-weekly extension lacks consensus.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **IL-6 blockade can suppress fever with infection:** warn patients to watch for infection symptoms without fever. Monitor blood pressure regularly.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tocilizumab (8 mg/kg every 2 weeks) is an alternative if siltuximab is unavailable,** but it is not PBS-funded for iMCD.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Steroids alone are not recommended:** they had the lowest response rate (2.8%).
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CDCN adjunct steroid doses:** for more indolent disease, prednisone 1 mg/kg or an equivalent steroid, given 4-8 weeks and then tapered; for more symptomatic disease, a higher start such as methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg with a slower taper. Stop steroids as early as possible once combined with other agents.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Rituximab 375 mg/m² for 4-8 doses is a first-line alternative (category 2B) for non-severe iMCD without marked cytokine-driven symptoms**, when a limited course is preferred to indefinite anti-IL-6 treatment. Evidence is thinner: CR 20% and PR 48% in one series, shorter progression-free survival than siltuximab, and about half fail in others.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Commonest siltuximab and tocilizumab side effects:** mild thrombocytopenia, raised triglycerides and cholesterol, and itch (CDCN). No trial has compared the two directly.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Dose interval (CDCN):** stopping anti-IL-6 treatment tends to bring relapse, so continue it indefinitely in responders; in the long-term siltuximab safety study, intervals were safely stretched to 6 weeks in 40% of patients.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe iMCD: escalate early (CDCN).** Start high-dose steroid (for example methylprednisolone 500 mg daily) with siltuximab, which may be given weekly for the first month; consider combination chemotherapy as soon as the patient worsens, or once 1 week of siltuximab has brought no response, whichever is sooner. Regimens used include R-CHOP, CVAD, CVP, VDT-ACE-R and etoposide/cyclophosphamide-based (HLH-type) regimens.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Fever and thrombocytopenia settle first,** often within a month on siltuximab; haemoglobin, CRP and albumin improve within 3 months; nodes can take 6–12 months. Weigh symptoms and organ recovery above nodal response.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review clinically and biochemically weekly until improving, then each 3-weekly cycle;** CT for nodal response at 6 and 12 months.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CDCN response criteria** combine three parts: biochemistry (haemoglobin, CRP, albumin, eGFR), lymph node size (modified Cheson) and four symptoms (fatigue, anorexia, fever, weight change, graded by CTCAE). Biochemical CR is normalisation of all values; PR is a 50% to 99% improvement in all; progression is a worsening of more than 25% in any. Overall CR needs CR in all three; any progression is overall progression.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Response categories in full (S1 Tables 9-10):** complete response means normal CRP, haemoglobin, albumin and GFR, a nodal complete response and symptoms back to baseline; partial response, more than 50% improvement in all four markers, a nodal partial response and improvement in all four symptom groups short of baseline; stable disease, under 50% improvement (or under 25% worsening) in the markers, no nodal response and improvement in some but not all symptoms; progression, more than 25% worsening of any marker, more than 25% nodal growth, or any symptom worse on 2 or more assessments. A symptom counts as improved with a fall of at least 1 CTC grade (fatigue, anorexia), a fall of at least 1°C (fever) or a weight gain of 5% or more.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Timing (CDCN):** symptoms should improve after 3 to 4 anti-IL-6 doses; follow haemoglobin, CRP, ESR and albumin weekly then fortnightly until normal. Nodes shrink slowly (median 5 months), so CT every 3 months until the best response, then every 6 and later 12 months. Siltuximab and tocilizumab falsely raise IL-6 for 18 to 24 months after the last dose, so IL-6 cannot measure response.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Poor response to steroids plus IL-6 blockade should prompt a diagnostic review.** Up to half of patients do not respond adequately to first-line therapy.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second line is rituximab-based** (Level IV, Grade C); chemotherapy such as CHOP or etoposide is reserved for severe, rapidly progressive disease. After chemoimmunotherapy that controls disease, continue siltuximab maintenance.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Third-line options:** thalidomide, anakinra, sirolimus or cyclosporin (the last especially in TAFRO); Level IV, Grade D. Prefer immunomodulatory therapy over chemotherapy where possible: toxicity is lower and efficacy similar.
claims.locator: Australasian multidisciplinary working group, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Australian clinical practice guideline: diagnosis and treatment of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 30 May 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13409200, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If anti-IL-6 treatment did not work first line, it need not be continued** (CDCN); after failure, re-check the diagnosis (for example lymphoma) before second-line rituximab-based therapy.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Why chemotherapy is held back (CDCN pooled data):** it had the highest response rate (78%) but relapses were common (42%) and toxicity significant, while immunomodulatory or immunosuppressive agents responded in 69%. Autologous or allogeneic transplant is a last resort with mixed results.
claims.locator: Castleman Disease Collaborative Network international working group (van Rhee F, Voorhees P, Dispenzieri A, et al.), Blood 132(20):2115-2124 (doi 10.1182/blood-2018-07-862334), 'International, evidence-based consensus treatment guidelines for idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease', published 4 September 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6238190/, retrieved 2026-09-24
